outcome: complications faced by CS and vaginal delivery
cohort: Mothers in select Indian states (Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu) with high institutional delivery rates (>95%).
finding: Preventable Caesarean section rates in the selected Indian states were significantly higher than the national average, with higher maternal education and middle socioeconomic status identified as key correlates.
mod_finding: The study identified considerably higher rates of preventable Caesarean sections, as defined by Robson's criteria, in the selected Indian states compared to the national level.
cross-section timing: Data from National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS-5)
